title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Let \hat\Pi_{0,3} be the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, a free profinite group on two generators. It sits as a normal subgroup of \hat\Gamma^+_{0,3}, the profinite completion of PSL(2,Z), written SL(2,Z)^{∧'} (the prime means 'mod ±1'). Here \Pi_{0,3} is Γ(2)/±1 and the quotient is S_3 = PSL(2,Z/2).

Grothendieck studies automorphisms u of \hat\Pi_{0,3} with these properties:
- u commutes up to inner automorphisms with the S_3-action, i.e. with the involution σ_∞ and the order-3 element ρ;
- u multiplies the inertia generators by an exponent μ ∈ \hat Z^*.
These are essentially GT-type elements (λ = μ, f), the solutions of the 'équation des lacets'. Such a u extends canonically to \hat\Gamma^+_{0,3}, inducing the identity on S_3.

The page continues the previous one, which hunted down a sign error. The first lines check the last entry of the commutator [u,ρ] computed there. They reduce the check to μ(u^2+t^2) = -1, which is the normalisation μ(u^2+t^2) = ε_2 in the case ε_2 = -1.

Theorem. Let f be the defining element of u and let its image in SL(2,\hat Z)/±1 be (r s; t u). Put ε_2 = ±1 with ε_2 ≡ μ mod 4, and (-1)^{α_2} = ε_2. Define
  \underline u = μ(t σ_∞ + u) τ_∞^{α_2} = μ (u t; -t u) diag(1, ε_2)^{α_2} = μ (u, ε_2 t; -t, ε_2 u).
Here u + t σ_∞ is a 'Gaussian integer' in the centraliser \hat Z[σ_∞] ≅ \hat Z[i] of σ_∞ = (0 1; -1 0), and τ_∞ = diag(1,-1) normalises it. Then:
- (76) det \underline u = μ;
- (77) \underline u σ_∞ \underline u^{-1} = ε_2 σ_∞;
- (78) \underline u ρ \underline u^{-1} = (ε_2 g) ρ, with g the element from formula (65).

Corollary. The action of u on PSL(2,Z)^∧ descends to the congruence quotient PSL(2,\hat Z) = SL(2,\hat Z)'. There it is the inner automorphism of GL(2,\hat Z) given by a matrix of determinant μ.

The next page adds that (t,u) is canonical up to sign. Replacing f by l_0^n f left-multiplies by (1 -2n; 0 1), which changes only the first row.

Purpose: to describe explicitly how GT (or the image of Gal(\bar Q/Q)) acts on the congruence quotient of the modular group, in terms of the multiplier μ. The underlying arithmetic is that μ^{-1}ε_2 = u^2 + t^2 is a norm from \hat Z[i].
errors: First line: with the factor read as (t-u), μu(u-t) = -(1+μt(t-u)) would give μ(u^2+t^2) - 2μut = -1, i.e. ut = 0 — the very contradiction met on the previous page. The bracket μ[u^2-ut+t^2+tu] = -1, which is marked 'o.K.', only follows if the factor is (t+u). So either the image reads (t+u) or there is a slip of sign; the intended identity is consistent.
Marginal formula '= (u, ε_2 t; -t, ε_2 u)' omits the overall factor μ.

(77) as written, '[\underline u, σ_∞] = ε_2·id', is a commutator taken in GL(2,\hat Z), valued in ±1. The check works: for α_2 = 0 the matrix commutes with σ_∞; for α_2 = 1, τ_∞ anticommutes with σ_∞. A possible leading dot or minus sign in the image should be ignored.
Corollary is stated loosely ('modulo signe' is added on the next page). The matrix is canonical only up to ±1, and up to the inner ambiguity f ↦ l_0^n f.

ideas.what: GT-type automorphisms of \hat F_2 (commuting with S_3, multiplier μ) extend to \widehat{PSL_2(Z)}. Their action on the congruence quotient PSL(2,\hat Z) is conjugation by an element of GL(2,\hat Z) of determinant μ.
ideas.modern_name: Action of \hat{GT} on the congruence completion of the modular group factors through the cyclotomic-type character λ (analogue of det of the Galois representation on modular curves)
ideas.usually_credited_to: For Galois: Shimura/Igusa (det = cyclotomic character on X(N)). For \hat{GT} acting on \widehat{SL_2(Z)}: discussed by Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura and others in the 1990s (exact attribution unsure).
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions \hat{SL_2(Z)} and the Teichmüller tower only in general terms; this explicit statement is unsure.

ideas.what: Explicit conjugating matrix \underline u = μ(t σ_∞ + u) τ_∞^{α_2}, built from the bottom row (t,u) of the congruence image of f. The constraint u^2 + t^2 = ε_2/μ with ε_2 ≡ μ mod 4 makes u + i t a 'Gaussian unit' of norm ε_2 μ^{-1} in \hat Z[i].
ideas.modern_name: Image of the GT parameter f in SL(2,\hat Z); norm form of the centraliser \hat Z[i] of the order-2 element

ideas.what: Invariance of (t,u) under f ↦ l_0^n f, which acts by the unipotent matrix (1 -2n; 0 1) (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Ambiguity of f modulo inertia at 0 / normalisation of tangential base point

missed.claim: An explicit formula for the induced action of a GT-type element (μ,f) on PSL(2,\hat Z) as inner conjugation by μ(u + tσ_∞)τ_∞^{α_2}. Here (t,u) is the bottom row of the image of f in SL(2,\hat Z), satisfying u^2 + t^2 = ε_2/μ and ε_2 ≡ μ mod 4.
missed.quote: cette dernière est induite par automorphisme intérieur de GL(2,\hat Z), défini par une \underline u \in GL(2,\hat Z) telle que det u = μ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The qualitative statement (action through det = λ) is known. An explicit canonical matrix in terms of f, valued in the norm group of \hat Z[i], is a concrete computational tool not standard in the GT literature.

missed.claim: Implicit link (not stated by Grothendieck): σ_∞ fixes λ = -1, where the Legendre curve is y^2 = x^3 - x with CM by Z[i]. The pair (u,t), a 'Gaussian integer' of norm ε_2μ^{-1}, should therefore match, for Galois elements, the Hecke character of this CM curve; likewise ρ ↔ j = 0 and Z[ζ_3]. The page does not say this; it is a reading of the formulas.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would tie the congruence image of the Drinfeld–Ihara f to CM Grössencharacters, in the same spirit as Anderson–Ihara's Jacobi-sum results for Fermat curves. It might also extend to define 'CM-type characters' on all of \hat{GT}.

deep.surprise_reason: That GT/Galois acts on the congruence quotient through a GL_2 element with determinant equal to the cyclotomic-type character is expected and essentially known. The explicit Gaussian-integer form of the conjugating matrix in terms of the congruence image of f is a nice unpublished detail, but it is likely recoverable by specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: for the 'o.K.' to hold, the right-hand side must be -(1+μt(t+u)), not (t-u). The next line, μ[u^2-ut+t^2+tu] = -1, is consistent with (t+u).
(75) margin: the bracketed '= (u, ε_2 t; -t, ε_2 u)' is a marginal addition, and the case-split display beneath it is struck out in the image.
(77): the image shows a small mark before ε_2 (possibly a dot or minus); mathematically it must be +ε_2.

Corollary: 'commutant extérieurement à \mathfrak S_3', 'μ son multiplicateur' (rather than 'μ "induit"'), and 'définie par une matrice \underline u' — the struck word under it is 'relation' or 'matrice'.
